Calibrate an RSYC Yield Curve with Local Observations

Source: R/calibrate_rsyc.R
calibrate_rsyc.Rd

Adjust a published RSYC curve to local field data using a best linear unbiased predictor (BLUP) of the local level. Given one or more observed values (aboveground biomass or total volume) at known stand ages, the function estimates a shrinkage-based local level adjustment and applies it as a multiplicative ratio to the selected national curve.

Usage

calibrate_rsyc(
  response,
  species,
  strata_level,
  strata_id,
  obs_age,
  obs_response,
  predict_age = NULL,
  apply_limits = TRUE,
  random_effect_limit_sd = 3,
  ratio_limit = 5,
  value_limit = 1000
)

Arguments

response

Forest measure to estimate: "agb" for aboveground biomass or "volume" for total volume.

species

A species code or broad group such as "coniferous". Uppercase and lowercase letters are treated the same.

strata_level

Type of area: "tile", "ecozone", "ecoprovince", "ecoregion", or "ecodistrict".

strata_id

Tile ID, ecological area name or path, or ecological code. Tile IDs, names, and paths are matched ignoring case. A single area name can be used when it occurs only once. If the name occurs in several places, use the full sequence of area names shown by rsyc_strata(). Numeric values are interpreted as codes for the selected ecological strata_level; quote ecoprovince codes such as "10.1".

obs_age

Stand ages, in years, of the local observations.

obs_response

Observed non-negative values at obs_age. Aboveground biomass in Mg/ha or total volume in m3/ha, matching response. Must be the same length as obs_age.

predict_age

One or more stand ages at which to return calibrated predictions. Defaults to the sorted unique obs_age.

apply_limits

When TRUE (the default), apply the safeguards that protect against implausible local adjustments: the random effect is constrained to random_effect_limit_sd standard deviations, an adjustment ratio above ratio_limit is discarded in favour of the bare curve, and any calibrated value above value_limit falls back to the bare curve. When FALSE, the raw shrunk BLUP adjustment is returned uncapped.

random_effect_limit_sd

Number of standard deviations of the local random-effect distribution at which the estimate is constrained. The default of 3 corresponds to the central 99.7% of that distribution. Only used when apply_limits is TRUE.

ratio_limit

Largest allowed calibration ratio before the adjustment is discarded. Only used when apply_limits is TRUE.

value_limit

Largest allowed calibrated value before the prediction falls back to the bare curve. Only used when apply_limits is TRUE.

Value

A list with the components:

predictions

A table of age and the calibrated value at each predict_age, together with the bare-curve value_uncalibrated.

ratio_blup

The multiplicative local adjustment applied to the curve.

b_pixel

The estimated pixel-level random effect \(\hat b_{ij}\) (capped and shrunk when apply_limits is TRUE).

shrinkage_factor

The shrinkage weight in [0, 1]; values near 0 mean weak local evidence pulled toward no adjustment.

n_obs

Number of observations used.

random_effect_limited, ratio_limited, value_limited

Flags indicating whether each safeguard altered the result.

model_id

Identifier of the national curve that was calibrated.

Details

The RSYC models are nonlinear mixed-effects models in which the tile- and pixel-level random effects act on \(\beta_1\), the parameter associated with the maximum biomass (or volume) potential (the asymptote parameter): $$AGB_{ijk} = (\beta_1 + b_i + b_{ij})\,g(age_{ijk}) + \epsilon_{ijk}$$ where \(i\) indexes the tile, \(j\) the pixel nested within the tile, \(k\) the age, and \(g(age) = e^{-\beta_4 age}(1 - e^{-\beta_2 age})^{\beta_3}\) is the age-related modifier. The random effects and residual errors are assumed to be independent and normally distributed with mean zero. Hats denote estimated values. The b1 coefficient published in RSYC_models is the tile-level asymptote parameter, already equal to \(\hat\beta_1 + \hat b_i\), so the yield curve based on the tile-level conditional prediction is \(\texttt{b1} \cdot \hat g(age)\).

Local calibration estimates the pixel-level random effect \(b_{ij}\) of the calibration plot (assumed to coincide with pixel \(j\) within tile \(i\)) conditional on the fitted model. Given observations \(y_{ijk}\) at ages \(age_{ijk}\), with \(m_{ijk} = \hat g(age_{ijk})\), $$\hat b_{ij} = \frac{\sum_k m_{ijk} (y_{ijk} - \texttt{b1} \cdot m_{ijk})}{\sum_k m_{ijk}^2 + \hat\sigma^2_\epsilon / \hat\sigma^2_b}$$ where \(\hat\sigma^2_b\) is the estimated pixel-level (nested within tile) random-effect variance and \(\hat\sigma^2_\epsilon\) is the estimated residual variance. The \(\hat\sigma^2_\epsilon / \hat\sigma^2_b\) term shrinks weak local evidence toward no adjustment. The calibrated curve substitutes the adjusted asymptote parameter into the same equation, $$(\texttt{b1} + \hat b_{ij})\,\hat g(age)$$ which is equivalent to scaling the published curve by \((\texttt{b1} + \hat b_{ij}) / \texttt{b1}\), reported as ratio_blup.

With a single observation this becomes a one-point level anchor. The result should be read as a single-observation BLUP-anchored RSYC curve, not as a local growth trajectory learned from the data.

References

Tompalski, P. et al. (2025). National remote sensing-derived aboveground biomass yield curves for Canada.

Examples

# One observation for a tile model selected by tile ID.
calibrate_rsyc(
  "agb", "PICE.MAR", "tile", "H14",
  obs_age = 45,
  obs_response = 65
)
#> $predictions
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>     age value value_uncalibrated
#>   <dbl> <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1    45  62.6               50.2
#> 
#> $ratio_blup
#> [1] 1.248941
#> 
#> $b_pixel
#> [1] 16.9871
#> 
#> $shrinkage_factor
#> [1] 0.8415476
#> 
#> $n_obs
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $random_effect_limited
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $ratio_limited
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $value_limited
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $model_id
#> [1] "rsyc_agb_national_tile_pice_mar_h14"
#> 

# Two observations for an ecoregion selected by numeric code.
calibrate_rsyc(
  "agb", "PICE.MAR", "ecoregion", 198,
  obs_age = c(45, 70),
  obs_response = c(52, 65)
)
#> $predictions
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>     age value value_uncalibrated
#>   <dbl> <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1    45  51.4               42.8
#> 2    70  64.2               53.5
#> 
#> $ratio_blup
#> [1] 1.198789
#> 
#> $b_pixel
#> [1] 11.62953
#> 
#> $shrinkage_factor
#> [1] 0.9291395
#> 
#> $n_obs
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $random_effect_limited
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $ratio_limited
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $value_limited
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $model_id
#> [1] "rsyc_agb_national_ecoregion_pice_mar_montane_cordillera_northern_montane_cordillera_skeena_mountains"
#> 

# Four observations for an ecodistrict selected by full hierarchy path.
calibrate_rsyc(
  "agb", "PICE.MAR", "ecodistrict",
  paste(
    "Atlantic Maritime", "Fundy Uplands", "Annapolis-Minas Lowlands",
    "Windsor Lowlands", sep = "/"
  ),
  obs_age = c(30, 50, 70, 90),
  obs_response = c(22, 31, 36, 39)
)
#> $predictions
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>     age value value_uncalibrated
#>   <dbl> <dbl>              <dbl>

#> 2    50  31.1               40.7
#> 3    70  36.5               47.8
#> 4    90  39.8               52.0
#>

#> [1] 0.7650299
#> 
#> $b_pixel
#> [1] -12.26633
#> 
#> $shrinkage_factor
#> [1] 0.9631163
#> 
#> $n_obs
#> [1] 4
#>
